image_description: A composite image displaying four different views of cast iron skillets. The top-left shows the bottom of a pan with a utensil holder in the background. The top-right shows the interior of a seasoned pan. The bottom-left shows the bottom of a pan with a large manufacturer's label/sticker. The bottom-right shows the interior of another seasoned pan. All pans exhibit the characteristic black, rough texture of cast iron.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All four panels clearly show circular pans where the diameter is significantly larger than the side height, consistent with a skillet.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Handles are visible in all quadrants. They are integrated into the body (typical of cast iron) and feature the standard hanging loop at the terminal end.
The transition from the flat bottom to the rim in the interior shots (top-right, bottom-right) shows the characteristic flare/slope of a frying pan.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The handles appear to be cast iron (same material as the pan body), which is a standard construction method for this class. No separate rivets are needed for one-piece casting, which is structurally valid.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bottom is flat (induction-compatible) or slightly rounded.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bottom-up views (top-left, bottom-left) show a generally flat surface suitable for stovetop contact.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows cooking residue patterns, oil sheen, or pristine non-stick coating.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cast iron (black, rough seasoned surface), stainless steel (polished silver), aluminum (brushed or anodized), or non-stick coated (black PTFE surface).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visual texture—pitted, dark grey/black, and heavy-looking—is unmistakably cast iron.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Material is metal with characteristic finish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Handle is proportionally sized for single-hand grip.
